scope: The 32 people, 53 relationships and 18 chronicle events currently used by the product. Legacy cultural/tribal articles and calendar rules are outside this review.
method: Read English and Cyrillic-Mongolian Wikipedia biographies/sections; compare only the facts named in each row. Interlanguage agreement is not independent historical proof. Preserve stronger existing sources when coverage differs.
languageReview: Traditional Mongolian text edits are limited to dates and short wording built from existing phrases. Native-speaker proofreading is pending; Wikipedia Cyrillic text is not mechanically transliterated.

people.facts: Temujin’s father; Hoelun’s husband; death in the late twelfth century. Exact year differs between the Mongolian lead and infobox.
Temujin’s mother and Yesugei’s wife; she raised the children after his death. Exact lifespan is not agreed across the two biographies.
Temujin/Genghis Khan; parents Yesugei and Hoelun; title and imperial foundation in 1206; died in 1227. Retain approximate birth year and no exact death day.
Genghis Khan’s principal wife; mother of Jochi, Chagatai, Ogedei and Tolui. Family and political role supported.
Borte’s eldest son, accepted by Genghis Khan; father of Batu and Berke. English death discussion gives 1225 or 1227, while Mongolian uses circa 1225 and 1225–1226 elsewhere.
Second son of Genghis Khan and Borte; Central Asian appanage; death in 1242.
Third son of Genghis Khan and Borte; elected in 1229 after Tolui’s regency; ruled until 1241. Use the Mongolian revision preceding the anomalous October edit.
Ogedei’s wife and Guyuk’s mother; administration between Ogedei’s death and Guyuk’s election. Leads use 1241–1246; infoboxes distinguish formal regency from 1242.
Fourth son of Genghis Khan and Borte; husband of Sorghaghtani; father of Mongke, Kublai, Hulegu and Ariq; regent during 1227–1229, later honored posthumously.
Tolui’s wife and mother of Mongke, Kublai, Hulegu and Ariq. Birth is placed in the late twelfth century; death in 1252.
Son of Ogedei and Toregene; reign 1246–1248, followed by Oghul Qaimish’s regency.
Son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani; reign 1251–1259; accession transferred the supreme title to Tolui’s line. Birth and exact coronation dates conflict inside the Mongolian page.
Son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani; born 1215, died 1294; rival elections in 1260; Great Yuan name in 1271; Southern Song defeated in 1279.
Kublai’s wife, Zhenjin’s mother; died in 1281. Political and religious influence supported; birth precision not increased.
Son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani; separately elected in 1260; war with Kublai ended with submission in 1264. Do not import judgments of exclusive legitimacy.
Son of Kublai and Chabi; father of Temur and Darmabala; died before Kublai. Crown-prince year is 1273 in English/Yuan shi versus 1274 in Mongolian.
Zhenjin’s third son and Kublai’s grandson; reign 1294–1307; brother of Darmabala.
Zhenjin’s second son; Temur’s elder brother; father of Qaishan. The posthumous imperial honor remains supported by English/Yuan shi, not established by the inspected Mongolian biography.
Darmabala’s son and Temur’s nephew; reign 1307–1311; father of Kusala.
Qaishan’s eldest son and Toghon Temur’s father; brief reign in 1329. Exact days vary within the Mongolian text; retain year precision.
Kusala’s son; reign began 1333; withdrew from Dadu in 1368; died 1370 and was succeeded by Ayushiridara. Describe the capital’s loss without asserting one uniform territorial endpoint.
Keraite ruler; Yesugei’s anda and Temujin’s early patron, later adversary.
Temujin’s anda, ally in the Merkit episode and later political/military rival.
Jochi’s son; supported Mongke’s accession. English describes the 1250/1251 election sequence; Mongolian supporting passages are less specific.
Son of Tolui and Sorghaghtani; campaign ordered by Mongke; founded the Ilkhanate; died 1265. English/Mongolian campaign-start dates differ (1253 mobilization versus 1255 dispatch).
Jochi’s son and Golden Horde ruler; war with Hulegu in 1262–1263. Keep the 1266/1267 end-date uncertainty; do not infer a direct succession from Batu.
Khabul’s father in the recorded genealogy. Exact dates and expanded Timurid genealogical traditions remain uncertain.
Tumbinai’s son, Bartan’s father and ruler of Khamag Mongol; Ambaghai succeeded him. Conflicting claims about other descendants are not imported.
Khabul’s son and Yesugei’s father. English evidence is in Yesugei/Khabul biographies, since the English Bartan title redirects to Yesugei.
Toghon Temur’s son; reign 1370–1378; Maidarbal’s father. Mongolian birth years disagree internally, so no exact birth year is added.

Ayushiridara’s son; captured by Ming forces in 1370 and returned north in 1374. English Maidilibala and Mongolian Ayushiridara support these episodes unevenly; identification with Elbeg remains a hypothesis.
Founder and emperor of Ming, reign 1368–1398. The two biographies do not establish the exact 1370 letter; existing Ming records remain necessary.

events.note: Poisoning tradition and late-twelfth-century placement agree; retain period precision because exact years differ.
Title and imperial foundation in 1206 agree.
Regency began after Genghis Khan’s death in 1227 and ended in 1229.
1229 election agrees with English and the reviewed Mongolian old revision.
1241–1246 describes the post-Ogedei interval; both infoboxes start formal regency in 1242. Retain the broad interval, not an exact accession day.
1251 accession and Toluid succession agree. Berke’s specific role is supported by English and existing primary/scholarly sources; not established by the inspected Mongolian passages.

English describes mobilization in 1253 and arrival in Transoxiana in 1255; Mongolian dates Mongke’s dispatch to 1255. The 1253 departure statement is not bilingually confirmed; retain the existing Yuan shi/Iranica sources for adjudication. Iranica was re-read: it explicitly dates departure to 1253 and arrival in Transoxania to 1255, supporting the existing wording.
Rival elections and war from 1260 to 1264 agree; omit judgments of one side’s exclusive legitimacy.
1262–1263 fighting agrees; the possible winter 1261–1262 start and relative weight of territorial/revenue causes still rely on existing Iranica scholarship.
Great Yuan dynastic name proclaimed in 1271 agrees.
Defeat of Southern Song in 1279 agrees.
Temur’s accession in 1294 after Kublai agrees; his father died before Kublai.
1368 withdrawal from Dadu and continuation of Toghon Temur’s reign until 1370 agree. Replaced the geographically overbroad statement.
Accession after his father’s death in 1370 agrees; do not add an exact day.
English Maidilibala records capture in Yingchang in 1370; Mongolian Ayushiridara identifies his captive son on release, without dating the capture. Existing Ming record retained.
The precise letter and its contents are not located in the two biographies. Keep the existing Ming Taizu shilu volume 57 citation; do not mark Wikipedia verification complete.
English Maidilibala and Mongolian Ayushiridara both record release/return in 1374; autumn detail remains tied to the existing Ming citation.
